title: Algebraic degree bound for bent functions
statement: Let $n$ be an even natural number with $2<n$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ be a Boolean function. If the real-valued function obtained by encoding $f(x)$ as $(-1)^{f(x)}$ is bent—that is, every Fourier coefficient indexed by a vector in the binary cube has absolute value $(2^{n/2})^{-1}$—then the algebraic degree of $f$ is at most $n/2$.
